close_reason: pkix-lint crate complete: traits + 6 CABF TLS BR lints + LintProfile; workspace green
description:
Everything is currently hard pass/fail: Result<ValidatedPath, Error>. There is no Warning, no advisory, no structured 'this cert would fail under profile X'. This means a profile cannot express 'this cert is technically valid per RFC 5280 but violates CABF BR §7.1.4.2' without throwing a hard error that aborts the chain.

A lint/diagnostic layer is needed for:
- Profile enforcement that distinguishes Error (reject) from Warn (log, don't reject)
- Compliance checking tools (would this cert pass issuance checks?)
- Audit trails (which rules were evaluated, which passed/warned/failed)
- Cross-profile contradiction surfacing (Profile A says X, Profile B says not-X)

Design requirements (informed by zlint lessons):
- Lint is the unit, Profile is a bundle of lints
- Each lint has: stable ID, citation (spec + version + section), severity, scope (cert vs path), subject kind (CA/subscriber/etc), effective TimeRange
- LintResult: Pass | NotApplicable | Warn(detail) | Error(detail) | Fatal(detail)
- Path-level lints receive the full ValidatedPath + policy tree, not just a single cert
- Runner takes a SystemTime for temporality — 'evaluate as of issuance time' vs 'evaluate now'
- Finding IDs must be stable across crate versions (treat as public API)

This is a significant new API surface. Scope for v0.2: define the traits and the runner; ship CABF TLS BR lints as the reference implementation. Defer FPKI/DoD/ETSI lint bundles to v0.3.

New crate: pkix-lint (engine + traits). pkix-profiles gains lint impls alongside the existing ValidationPolicy factories.
title: pkix: add lint/diagnostic layer — structured soft-fail and advisory results
